messages:
morgan: quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak we rolled last night host CPU on grpc-ingress jumped ~18% and p95 for short sequences (<64 tokens) went from ~40ms -> ~95ms.

morgan: short profile (pprof top, sampled across ingress hosts):
```
23.4%  parse_request
18.1%  grpc_writev
12.7%  tokenization::tokenize_batch
11.6%  kvcache::lookup_miss
9.9%   kernel_batch::compute
```

priya: is this aligned with the batch hint change? i thought we nudged soft_batch_target up to favor throughput.

morgan: yeah — kernel-selector now prefers kernel_A for mixed-length which implicitly ups the per-kernel batch target ~4x. hypothesis: for short requests this increases interleaving of different prefixes and evicts kv cache entries more often.

daniel: confirmed in traces: kvcache miss rate jumped from ~8% -> ~25% on affected nodes. grpc writev calls per minute 120k -> 720k (6x). also saw HTTP/2 frame count per stream increase.

tasha: ouch. can we rollback selector quickly? or hotpatch chunker to coalesce writes? small writes are killing host CPU.

morgan: I pushed a temporary traffic split back to kernel_B for short-seq routes around 01:30 and CPU dropped back ~12% within 5m. easy rollback if we want to revert rollout.

priya: long-term fixes proposed:
- cap kernel batch target on sequences < 64 tokens
- enable prefix-pin heuristic in kvcache (pin short-prefixes to avoid churning)
- add writev coalescing in sidecar proxy for streaming chunks (combine small frames into a single write)
- add an ingress http2 coalesce knob (configurable by route)

daniel: added checklist and owners:
- cap batch size for short seqs — @priya
- kvcache prefix-pin implementation — @daniel
- sidecar writev coalesce + tests — @tasha
- observability: add kvcache miss rate dashboard and per-route writev counter — @morgan

perf-bot: deploy recorded: kernel-selector v2.3.1 -> v2.3.2 at 2026-03-19T02:12:07Z (rolled back partially at 2026-03-19T01:30:22Z)

deploy-bot: rollback applied to route: /v1/generate (short-seq traffic split 80/20 -> kernel_B/kernel_A)

tasha: I'll prototype writev coalescer today. quick question — any existing edge cases with large streaming responses? want to ensure we don't regress tail latency for long seqs.

priya: add a max buffer time (5ms) and max coalesce size (8KB). that should keep long-seq unaffected.

morgan: thanks — let's keep the temp split until the cap+pin are in. will update on perf dashboard tomorrow.
